milestones.title: M1 — Desktop foundation
milestones.objective: Stand up the Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript shell with system tray, window lifecycle, local settings persistence, logging, and the base app layout matching the Pi Control design reference.

milestones.title: M2 — Device registry and SSH connectivity
milestones.objective: Let the user register, edit, and remove devices; connect to them over Windows OpenSSH with proper timeout/authentication/host-key error classification; persist devices.json.

milestones.title: M3 — Monitoring engine
milestones.objective: Collect system metrics and Docker container status per device over SSH, build immutable snapshots, and run a bounded-concurrency scheduler with manual and automatic refresh and partial-failure isolation.

milestones.title: M4 — Desktop experience
milestones.objective: Deliver the final dashboard, device detail, services, and settings screens matching the Pi Control design, plus terminal/service launching, deduplicated notifications, and autostart.

milestones.title: M5 — Post-MVP backlog (Phase 2)
milestones.objective: Ship a distributable production build, then work through the explicitly-deferred Phase 2 enhancements: Docker container lifecycle actions, an embedded terminal, and per-event-type notification controls.

milestones.title: M6 - Device Health and Diagnostics
milestones.objective: Extend monitoring into deterministic device health, Raspberry Pi power/throttling interpretation, and read-only connectivity diagnostics.

milestones.title: M7 - Service Health and Operational Activity
milestones.objective: Add service health monitoring and bounded operational activity.

milestones.title: M8 - Alerts and Threshold Governance
milestones.objective: Add governed alerts and configurable threshold policies.

milestones.title: M10 - Controlled Device Administration
milestones.objective: Add controlled restart and shutdown actions; remote power-on remains out of scope.

milestones.title: M11 - Network, Storage, and System Visibility
milestones.objective: Expose richer device-level network, storage, and system context.

milestones.title: M12 - Historical Monitoring
milestones.objective: Add bounded historical health monitoring after current-state contracts stabilize.

milestones.title: M13 - Document Hygiene
milestones.objective: Perform a final documentation-quality and governance-reconciliation pass.

milestones.title: M10 — Controlled Device Administration
milestones.objective: Deliver four typed, safety-governed administration operations without generic remote execution.

milestones.title: M11 — Network, Storage, and System Visibility
milestones.objective: Expose read-only network, storage, and system context in Device Details.

milestones.title: M12 — Historical Monitoring
milestones.objective: Add bounded local historical monitoring for device, service, and container operational trends.

milestones.title: M13 Document Hygiene
milestones.objective: Reconcile Pi-Hub documentation with the product and repository implemented through M12.

milestones.title: M14 Performance Benchmarking, Runtime Hardening & Device Detail UX
milestones.objective: Establish opt-in, bounded in-application performance diagnostics; harden runtime behavior; and reorganize Device Detail with tab-scoped data loading.

Repository layout matches the structure documented in docs/pi-hub-technical-architecture-specification.md section 27

workUnits.title: Local settings persistence and logging foundation
workUnits.objective: Implement versioned JSON storage for config.json with atomic writes plus a rotating local log, and expose get_app_settings/save_app_settings commands.

config.json schema with schemaVersion, refreshIntervalSeconds, startWithWindows, minimizeToTray, notificationsEnabled, theme

Recovery behavior when config.json is missing or corrupted

A corrupted config.json does not crash the app; it recovers to defaults and logs a warning
No secrets or private-key content ever appear in logs

Visual style (colors, spacing, typography) matches the Pi Control Claude Design reference

acceptanceCriteria: Devices persist across an application restart
devices.json includes schemaVersion and validates on load

workUnits.title: Device CRUD commands and validation
workUnits.objective: Implement create_device / update_device / delete_device commands with strict input validation for host, port, username, and service URLs.
scope: Validation for hostname/IPv4/IPv6/MagicDNS, SSH port range, Linux username, and http/https-only service URLs
create_device / update_device / delete_device Tauri commands wired to the device repository
Frontend-safe ApplicationError model (code, message, remediation, retryable)
outOfScope: SSH connectivity test itself (next work unit)
acceptanceCriteria: Invalid host/port/username/service URL values are rejected with a clear ApplicationError
Shell metacharacters in any field are rejected

workUnits.title: SSH adapter and remote command catalogue
workUnits.objective: Implement controlled process execution of the Windows OpenSSH client with a fixed RemoteOperation catalogue (Probe, SystemIdentity, SystemMetrics, DockerContainers) and hard timeouts.
scope: RemoteExecutor trait + Windows OpenSSH process-based implementation using BatchMode=yes and ConnectTimeout
RemoteExecutionResult struct (exit_code, stdout, stderr, duration_ms, timed_out)
Error classification: DnsResolutionError, ConnectionTimeout, ConnectionRefused, AuthenticationError, HostKeyError, RemoteCommandError, RemoteCommandTimeout
Arguments passed as separate process args, never string-interpolated
acceptanceCriteria: A fake RemoteExecutor can be substituted in tests to simulate online, offline, timeout, authentication failure, and host-key failure
Host-key errors are never auto-resolved or bypassed
Every remote execution enforces a hard timeout

workUnits.title: Connection testing command and device forms UI
workUnits.objective: Wire test_device_connection into the backend/frontend and build the add/edit/delete device forms styled per the Pi Control device-settings screen.
scope: test_device_connection Tauri command using the SSH adapter's probe operation
Add/Edit/Delete device forms (name, hostname, SSH user, port, description, device type, refresh interval, monitoring/notifications toggles)
Connection status feedback in the UI (online/offline/authentication_error/host_key_error/timeout/unknown)
outOfScope: System metrics or Docker data display (M3/M4)
acceptanceCriteria: Raspberry Pi 2 and Raspberry Pi 5 can be registered, edited, and deleted end-to-end through the UI
Connection test results distinguish authentication failure from host-key failure in the UI
No SSH password is ever requested or stored

workUnits.title: Remote system metrics collection and parsing
workUnits.objective: Collect CPU, memory, disk, temperature, uptime, load average, model, OS, kernel, and architecture in one SSH session using a stable key-value payload, and parse it defensively.
scope: SystemMetrics remote operation reading /proc/stat (CPU delta), /proc/meminfo, /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone0/temp, root filesystem disk usage, uname-derived identity fields
PIHUB_* key-value parser: ignore unknown fields, reject invalid numeric values, preserve valid fields, return partial warnings
SystemMetrics domain struct with optional fields for anything that may be unavailable
acceptanceCriteria: Missing/optional fields (e.g. temperature) never fail the whole metrics collection
Malformed key-value lines produce warnings without discarding valid fields
Rust unit tests cover well-formed, partially-malformed, and empty payloads

workUnits.title: Docker discovery and container parsing
workUnits.objective: Detect Docker availability and list containers read-only via `docker ps -a --no-trunc --format '{{json .}}'`, parsing each line independently.
scope: Container listing command and JSON-lines parser producing DockerContainerSummary (name, image, state, statusText, health, ports)
Malformed lines create warnings without discarding valid entries
dockerAvailable=false path when Docker is missing or the SSH user lacks permission, without marking the device offline
outOfScope: Any container start/stop/restart/exec (explicitly out of MVP scope)
acceptanceCriteria: A device with Docker unavailable still reports online with valid system metrics
A Docker permission error is classified as DockerPermissionError and does not fail the whole device refresh
Rust unit tests cover well-formed, malformed, and empty docker ps output

workUnits.title: Monitoring scheduler, snapshots, and bounded concurrency
workUnits.objective: Build the refresh lifecycle: probe, collect metrics, collect Docker data, assemble an immutable DeviceSnapshot, and run it on a scheduler with bounded concurrency and manual/automatic refresh.
scope: DeviceSnapshot domain struct (connectionStatus, capturedAt, durationMs, metrics, dockerAvailable, containers, warnings, error)
Scheduler with configurable interval (default 60s, 15-3600s range), max 4 concurrent refreshes, one active refresh per device
Backend events: device://snapshot-updated, device://status-changed, container://status-changed, monitoring://refresh-started, monitoring://refresh-completed
state.json persistence of last-known snapshots (non-authoritative; app must work if deleted)
acceptanceCriteria: A failing/offline device does not stop the scheduler or block other devices' refreshes
Manual refresh and automatic refresh both work without freezing the UI
Stale snapshots remain visible with an explicit stale marker and last-refresh timestamp after a failed refresh
Deleting state.json does not prevent the app from starting

workUnits.title: Status-transition detection and notification decisions
workUnits.objective: Compare consecutive snapshots to detect device and container state transitions and decide when a notification should fire, with deduplication persisted across restarts.
scope: Device transition rules: online<->offline, online->authentication_error, online->host_key_error
Container transition rules: running->exited/stopped/restarting/unhealthy (skip containers already stopped when first discovered)
Deduplication key: deviceId + resourceId + previousState + currentState, persisted in state.json
NotificationService trait producing notification-ready events (actual OS notification dispatch happens in M4)
acceptanceCriteria: Repeated refreshes with an unchanged state never produce duplicate notification events
A container already stopped at first discovery does not trigger a notification
Rust unit tests cover each transition rule and the dedup key

workUnits.objective: Allow starting, stopping, and restarting a device's Docker containers from the container table, with explicit confirmation, lifting the MVP's read-only-only Docker constraint for these three actions.

Tauri commands with device/container id validation and confirmation-required semantics

workUnits.objective: Add an in-app SSH terminal pane (matching the Pi Control design's terminal modal) as an alternative to shelling out to an external terminal application.

workUnits.title: Per-event-type notification controls
workUnits.objective: Replace the single per-device notificationsEnabled toggle with separate, independently-backed rules for offline transitions, container failures, and high resource usage, matching the design mockup's three switches with real behavior behind each.
scope: Extend the notification domain model with per-category enable flags
Gate WU012's transition rules by the relevant category instead of one global per-device flag
Device settings UI: three real toggles instead of the current single simplified one
outOfScope: Custom user-defined notification rules beyond the three built-in categories
acceptanceCriteria: Disabling only the offline-transition category suppresses device online/offline notifications but not container ones, and vice versa
Existing dedup guarantees (WU012) continue to hold per category

workUnits.title: Single-instance guard and autostart launch visibility
workUnits.objective: Make Pi-Hub genuinely 'invisible' in normal background use: prevent a second concurrent process from ever starting, and confirm (fixing if needed) that an autostart launch never visibly flashes the main window before hiding it.
scope: Register tauri-plugin-single-instance so a second launch focuses/shows the existing instance's tray-owned window instead of starting a second process
Verify (and fix if reproducible) whether the main window is visible for any frame between window creation and the --minimized hide() call in setup()
If a visible flash is reproducible, prevent it via the window's initial visibility configuration rather than a post-creation hide()
outOfScope: Any other performance work beyond these two specific issues (already measured as good: ~70MB idle working set, <1% average CPU with a device on a 15s refresh interval)
acceptanceCriteria: Launching Pi-Hub while it is already running never results in two pi-hub.exe processes; the existing instance's window is shown/focused instead
An autostart (--minimized) launch never shows the main window, even momentarily, before it settles into the tray

workUnits.title: Branded fallback page for webview load failures
workUnits.objective: Replace WebView2's native browser-style network-error page with a small Pi-Hub-branded fallback if the main window's content ever fails to load, so a load failure never looks like a stray browser error inside the app.
scope: A minimal static fallback.html matching the app's dark theme and pi badge, with a Retry button

Hook WebView2's NavigationCompleted event (Windows-only) via Tauri's with_webview escape hatch; on a failed navigation, navigate to the fallback page instead of leaving WebView2's own error chrome visible
outOfScope: Automatic retry/reconnect logic beyond the user-triggered Retry button
Any fix to the underlying cause of a specific load failure (out of scope: this is a presentation-layer safety net, not a root-cause fix)
acceptanceCriteria: Simulating a load failure (unreachable devUrl on a debug build) shows the branded fallback page, not WebView2's native error page
A normal successful load (dev and release) is completely unaffected by the hook

workUnits.title: In-app update checking and installation
workUnits.objective: Let the user update Pi-Hub from inside the app (checking a GitHub Releases-hosted manifest, downloading, and installing a newer signed build) instead of always needing a manually rebuilt and reinstalled MSI/NSIS package.
scope: tauri-plugin-updater integration, with an update signing keypair (private key kept out of the repository)
GitHub Releases as the update artifact/manifest host, with a documented (or scripted) process for publishing a signed release
Global settings: a real 'Check for updates' control replacing the disabled placeholder, with checking/downloading/ready-to-restart states
outOfScope: Automated CI/CD build pipeline (e.g. GitHub Actions) for producing releases -- releases are built and published the same way every other build in this project has been, not by a new automated pipeline
Auto-check on a background schedule -- MVP is a manual, user-triggered check only
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking 'Check for updates' with no newer release available reports that clearly, without error
A published newer release can be downloaded and installed from inside the app, and the app relaunches on the new version
The update artifact's signature is verified before installing; an unsigned or tampered artifact is rejected

workUnits.title: Persist recent device activity across restarts
workUnits.objective: Make the device detail screen's 'Recent Activity' feed survive an app restart instead of always starting empty, since notification-worthy transitions are currently only held in memory for the running session.

Keep the existing live-update behavior via notification://ready unchanged for the running session

acceptanceCriteria: Closing and reopening the app still shows the device's most recent activity entries, not an empty feed
The persisted log stays bounded (does not grow without limit) across long-running use

workUnits.title: Actionable Windows notifications
workUnits.objective: Clicking a Pi-Hub desktop notification currently does nothing; it should bring the app to the foreground and navigate to the relevant device, closing the loop between 'device went offline' and actually looking at it.
scope: Wire a click handler on notifications dispatched from src-tauri/src/platform/notifications.rs so clicking one shows the main window and routes the frontend to that device's detail screen
Carry the device id through the notification payload/action needed to do this

Dismissing a notification without clicking it has no side effects

workUnits.title: Terminal reconnect on disconnect

scope: Add a 'Reconnect' control shown in a terminal window's closed/error state, reusing openTerminalSession for the same device

Reconnecting does not create a duplicate/orphaned PTY session on the Rust side

workUnits.title: Remember terminal window position and size per device
workUnits.objective: Each terminal window currently opens centered with a small cascade offset and forgets its geometry on close, so a user who regularly reopens the same device's terminal has to re-drag/resize it every time.
scope: Persist each device's last terminal window position and size (e.g. in src/stores/useTerminalSessions.tsx or local settings storage)
Use the remembered geometry as the initial position/size the next time that device's terminal is opened, falling back to the current centered/cascaded default when there is none yet

acceptanceCriteria: Dragging/resizing a device's terminal, closing it, and reopening it later restores the last position and size

workUnits.title: Dynamic tray icon for offline/unhealthy devices
workUnits.objective: The tray icon is currently static regardless of fleet health; since Pi-Hub is designed to live in the tray, badging or swapping the icon when any monitored device is offline or unhealthy lets the user notice at a glance without opening the window.
scope: Add an alternate tray icon (or badge overlay) used when at least one monitoring-enabled device is offline, in an error state, or has an unhealthy/failed container
Update the tray icon reactively from the existing device://status-changed / container://status-changed events the scheduler already emits
Revert to the normal icon once every device is healthy again
outOfScope: Per-device icon variants or a menu bar summary beyond the single glanceable icon state
acceptanceCriteria: The tray icon visibly changes within one refresh cycle of a monitored device going offline or a container becoming unhealthy
The tray icon returns to its normal state once the underlying issue clears

workUnits.title: Instant refresh after a Docker container action
workUnits.objective: After starting/stopping/restarting a container, the UI currently just says the dashboard will reflect the result on the next scheduled refresh (up to several minutes by default), giving no immediate confirmation the action worked.

Changing the scheduled background refresh interval itself
acceptanceCriteria: Starting, stopping, or restarting a container updates that device's snapshot (and the visible container state) within a couple of seconds, without waiting for the device's normal refresh interval
A failed action does not trigger a false 'success' refresh

scope: Add a bounded log-fetch remote operation (e.g. docker logs --tail N) to the existing SSH remote command catalogue

acceptanceCriteria: From a device's container list, the user can view that container's most recent bounded log output on demand
Fetching logs for a container with little/no output, or an unreachable device, fails gracefully with a clear message rather than hanging or crashing

Distinguish a device using its own override from one using the global default interval

Changing the refresh interval from this indicator (editing stays in DeviceForm)
acceptanceCriteria: A device with a custom refresh interval visibly shows that it differs from the global default
The indicator reflects a reasonable estimate of time until the next automatic refresh

delete_device: removes by id, NotFound if nothing was removed.
